lesson.summary: EC2 offers several ways to pay. On-Demand has no commitment and bills for the time an instance runs. Savings Plans and Reserved Instances give lower rates in exchange for a one or three year commitment. Spot Instances use spare capacity at a steep discount but can be interrupted. Dedicated Hosts give you a whole physical server for compliance or licensing needs.
keyPoints: On-Demand: no commitment, pay for the time an instance runs, suits short or unpredictable workloads
Savings Plans: commit to a steady amount of spend for one or three years for a lower rate
Reserved Instances: commit to one or three years of a specific configuration for a lower rate
Spot Instances: spare capacity at a large discount that can be interrupted, so use them for fault-tolerant or flexible work
Dedicated Hosts: a whole physical server for exclusive use, with control over instance placement, for compliance or licensing
Dedicated Instances: isolated hardware, but you do not choose which physical server they run on
Capacity Reservations hold capacity in an Availability Zone; they do not give a discount on their own
lesson.simpleSummary: EC2 has several ways to pay. On-Demand is pay as you go with no promise. Savings Plans and Reserved Instances are cheaper if you promise to use them for one or three years. Spot is very cheap but can be taken back at short notice. Dedicated Hosts give you a whole physical server.
lesson.mnemonic: Naruto hint: Pay as you go is like buying ramen at the stall, one bowl at a time. A promise for a year or three is like Ichiraku's membership card: cheaper, but you have to keep coming back.

scenarios.text: A company runs a steady production database on EC2 that it expects to need for the next three years. It also runs a nightly batch job that can restart from the beginning if it is interrupted.

questions.prompt: Which pricing option has no long-term commitment and charges for the time an instance runs?
questions.explanation: On-Demand Instances have no commitment and bill for the time they run. Dedicated Hosts are a physical server option, Reserved Instances need a long commitment, and Capacity Reservations hold capacity without giving a discount on their own.
questions.simplePrompt: Which pricing option has no promise and charges for the time a server runs?
questions.simpleExplanation: On-Demand. You pay for the time the server runs, with no long-term promise.

questions.prompt: Which TWO options lower the rate for a steady workload in exchange for a one or three year commitment? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Savings Plans and Reserved Instances both trade a one or three year commitment for a lower rate. Spot Instances carry no commitment and can be interrupted, and On-Demand has no discount for commitment.
questions.simplePrompt: Which two options are cheaper for a steady workload if you promise one or three years?
questions.simpleExplanation: Savings Plans and Reserved Instances. You promise to use them for a long time, and you pay less.

questions.prompt: Which pricing choice best fits the nightly batch job in this scenario?

options.text: Spot Instances, because the job can restart after an interruption
Dedicated Hosts, because the job must never be interrupted
Three-year Reserved Instances for the batch job only
On-Demand Instances, because Spot Instances cannot run batch work

questions.explanation: Spot Instances use spare capacity at a large discount and suit fault-tolerant work that can restart. Dedicated Hosts are not needed for a restartable job, and Spot Instances can run batch work.
questions.simplePrompt: Which pricing choice fits a nightly batch job that can restart if it is stopped?
questions.simpleExplanation: Spot Instances. They are very cheap, and a job that can restart is fine if the server is taken back.

questions.statement: Spot Instances are a good choice for a critical workload that cannot be interrupted.
questions.explanation: False. Spot Instances can be reclaimed by AWS when the capacity is needed, so they suit fault-tolerant or flexible work rather than critical workloads that cannot be interrupted.
questions.simplePrompt: True or false: Spot Instances are good for a critical job that must never stop.
questions.simpleExplanation: False. Spot servers can be taken back at short notice, so they are for jobs that can restart.

questions.prompt: A financial company must run workloads on a physical server it controls, including where instances are placed, for compliance reasons. Which option fits best?
questions.explanation: Dedicated Hosts give exclusive use of a physical server and control over instance placement, which fits compliance needs. Spot, On-Demand and Savings Plans are pricing models on shared infrastructure, not control over the physical server.
questions.simplePrompt: A financial company must control the physical server and where its servers are placed, for compliance. Which option fits?
questions.simpleExplanation: Dedicated Hosts. You get a whole physical server just for you, so you control where things run.
